title: rules the model only follows become checks a script makes
description: Tasks, one rule per task, each deleting its prose: (1) audit-task start refuses a task that is not ready unless --force, which journals the exception. (2) Phase status and claim are written by a verb, not a hand edit. (3) executor.runsGate is resolved by a script, not by the model reading config. Measure the mandatory-read bytes of /audit:next before and after each. Waits for the pipeline pilot in the measurement phase.
desiredOutcome: the first rules the orchestrator prose asks the model to follow are made by scripts instead, each with a test and with its prose section deleted, and the bytes an execution command must read go down with each move

findings.issue: A phase claim has no liveness: _claim_plan returns contested for any claim whose sessionId differs from the current one, and only sign-off or cancel clears it, so ordinary multi-session use of a sharded plan is refused - the next /audit:next session continuing a phase, every /audit:resume after a crash or lost session, a session id change across a resume, and (with no session id) a held claim even --force cannot replace - making --force the normal way to continue a phase and a forced row no longer an exception.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.4-b6f (fca3219f): Refuse only when the holder may still be live: when no live run holds the phase-<id> lock (the _locks liveness answer audit-lock status gives), take the claim over without --force and record it on the task.start row as a takeover with that basis; refuse, with --force as the way past, only when a live holder exists or liveness cannot be asked; decide and test the no-session path explicitly; cases for a sequential second session (takeover) and a live holder (refused).

findings.issue: The orchestrator flow says nothing about what to do on the new readiness and claim refusals, while both refusal texts offer --force --reason as the next step and task.md calls --force the route for promoting a task by hand, inviting a model mid-run to add --force with a reason in its own words rather than the operator's.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.5-b6f (c3482e27): On a readiness or claim refusal the orchestrator stops and relays the refusal verbatim; --force only on the human's instruction with the human's words as --reason (the operator's-words rule); reword both refusal texts to name the operator's decision before the flag; task.md describes --force as the operator's exception.

findings.issue: With no session id and another session's claim held, a forced start keeps the claim but still reports claimReplaced and writes 'FORCED past ... claim of session X' as if it had been replaced.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.4-b6f (fca3219f): Set replaced only when a claim was written in its place, word the no-session force as kept, and pin claimReplaced None with the claim byte-identical.

findings.issue: The claim's sessionId is the raw CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, unsanitised and unbounded, written into a committed shard and the task.start row, while _journal_io.env_session_id() exists to bound exactly this value; the journal actor and the claim can spell one session two ways.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.4-b6f (fca3219f): Use _journal_io.env_session_id() for the claim write and the holder comparison, with a case for an over-long or unsafe value.

findings.issue: run.md step 4 'Unmet blockers -> refuse and list them' still asks the model to apply the readiness rule by hand, a second copy of the rule start now enforces.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.5-b6f (c3482e27): Point it at the start refusal and say to relay it.

findings.issue: Deleting sub-steps a and d left step 1 as a paragraph followed by a lone 'b.-c.' sub-item.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.5-b6f (c3482e27): Fold the b-c text into step 1 or re-letter it, keeping the citations that point at it true.

findings.issue: On the sharded layout a claim on an index stub is a fallback when the shard has none; start writes the shard and sign-off pops the assembled claim, so a legacy stub claim survives sign-off and reappears as another session's claim.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.4-b6f (fca3219f): Have sign-off and cancel also drop a stub claim on the index under the index lock, or stop reading stub claims once a shard exists.

findings.issue: start reads an absent phase lock as proof nobody runs the phase, so a live session that started by hand (/audit:task start takes no phase lock) has its claim silently taken over by the next session, the orchestrated path too (its acquire succeeds because the hand starter holds no lock), and a claim pulled from another clone is always read as unheld; the takeover line says the holder 'holds no live run', which an absent lock cannot establish.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.6-b6f (791d8387): Give every claim readable liveness: start takes a hand-off phase-<id> lock (recording CLAUDE_PID as audit-lock acquire does) when it writes a claim and none is held, so a hand start leaves the evidence an orchestrated one does; until a claim carries that evidence, treat none under another session's claim as unaskable unless this run holds the lock; word the takeover as its basis ('no live phase-<id> lock in this clone'); a case where a hand start with a live pid and no lock makes the next session refuse.

findings.issue: A holder judged dead by the age rule alone (a lock with no pid, or from another host, older than the age limit) is taken over with no human involved, while audit-lock acquire treats the same verdict as exit 4 and its protocol asks the human before --takeover.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.6-b6f (791d8387): Map a not-live verdict whose basis is the age fallback (no pid probed) to unaskable; keep dead for a pid gone on this host and the empty interrupted take; cases for a no-pid and an other-host lock past the age limit, both refusing.

findings.issue: task.md's claim prose drifted from the code: an unconditional refusal still listed, 'only when that other session still runs a live lock' where the code refuses any live lock this run does not hold, no mention of the no-session keep, and the --json keys omit claimKept and claimHolder.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.7-b6f (2aa81131): Make each sentence true of _claim_plan and _claim_refusal, and list every --json key the start result carries.

findings.issue: The relay-and-force rule is written three times in the files /audit:next must read (plus run.md and task.md), raising those bytes, while no script can tell an operator's --reason from the model's - a prose-only rule in the phase that exists to remove them.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.7-b6f (2aa81131): State it once where the operator's-words rule lives and point to it elsewhere, recovering the bytes; record that it is a prose-only rule until a mechanism reads the reason from the operator's own prompt.

findings.issue: A keep start does no lock work, so liveness is written once and never refreshed: a session that resumes under a new process leaves its lock naming a dead pid and another session's start takes the claim and lock over while it still runs, and a keep start ignores another session's live phase lock, so both sessions run the phase.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.8-b6f (aa375390): Run _take_phase_lock on keep too, so another run's live lock refuses a keep start; in the ours branch, re-take the lock for this run when its recorded pid is gone or differs from the current process, so the lock names the live process. Cases: a same-session start under a new process after the old one died, then another session's start, refused; a keep start while another session's live lock is held, refused.

findings.issue: held_by_us reads a handed-off lock as ours on a session match alone even when its recorded pid is gone, so acquire answers 'already yours' to a resumed session over a lock every other reader judges dead.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.8-b6f (aa375390): Refresh the recorded pid on a same-session re-entry whose recorded pid is gone, through the same re-take the start's ours branch uses.

findings.issue: After a hand start takes the start lock, the same session's orchestrator acquire answers exit 5 and leaves it, and sign-off then releases it by its start note, so the merge runs with no phase lock held while the orchestrator believes it holds one.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.8-b6f (aa375390): When the orchestrator's acquire meets a start-noted lock of its own session, re-take it under the orchestrator's note so the start-note release leaves it; a case runs hand start, orchestrator acquire, sign-off, and finds the lock still held.

findings.issue: A sign-off or cancel by a session that never held the start lock, while the starting session is live, prints release_refusal's takeover text telling the operator another session took the lock over and to re-read their writes, though nothing was taken over.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.8-b6f (aa375390): Print this function's own wording naming the live holder and saying the lock was left in place; keep the takeover text for a run that actually held the lock.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py start, between the lock take and the guarded write
findings.issue: Calls between taking the lock and the first guarded write are not covered by undo_lock, so an exception there leaves a lock under the live process that refuses every other session until it ends.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.8-b6f (aa375390): Take the lock immediately before the writing try, or wrap the span from take to validated write so undo_lock runs and the exception re-raises.

findings.issue: _holder_gone calls two private helpers of _locks, so a rename inside _locks silently breaks a second module.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.8-b6f (aa375390): Expose one public predicate in _locks that judge and the release conflict also use, and call it from audit-task.

findings.issue: The paragraph says a start takes the claim over whenever the holder's lock is not live, but no lock in this clone and an age-only lock are refused as unaskable; a takeover happens only on a lock observed gone or on this run's own live lock.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.9-b6f (4733c18e): Name the takeover conditions as the code decides them and say that no lock and an age-only lock are refused as unaskable.

findings.issue: The line says resume's start takes a dead holder's lock over itself, but resume first acquires the phase lock and a dead holder answers exit 4, which stops for the human before a --takeover rerun; start's own takeover belongs to a hand-typed start.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.9-b6f (4733c18e): Say resume takes the dead lock over through its own acquire after the human confirms exit 4, that start then reuses that lock, and that start's own takeover is for a hand-typed start.

findings.issue: The --force paragraph still restates the relay rule that now lives once in manifest-conventions.md.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.9-b6f (4733c18e): Replace the clause with the pointer the other call sites use and keep only the flag mechanics.

findings.issue: The left-in-place wording covers only a holder judge reads as live: a start lock judged by age alone (no pid, another host, an unprobeable pid) falls through to release_refusal's text telling the operator another session took the lock over and to re-read their writes, which is false because this session never held it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.10-b6f (a87c0cf0): Decide on taken_from alone: without it, always print the left-in-place sentence naming the holder and the judge basis; keep the takeover sentence for taken_from; cases with a pid-less aged lock and a foreign-host lock.

findings.issue: A resumed run's preflight acquire re-records its own gone-pid lock and answers already-yours with 'not this call's to give back', so an orchestrator following its guidance never releases it and the merged phase stays locked against other sessions while the resumed process lives, then needs a human-confirmed takeover.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.10-b6f (a87c0cf0): When the acquire is handed off, treat re-recording a gone pid as this call's hold: return 0, carry the token and say it was re-recorded from a gone pid; keep already-yours for non-handed-off callers and refresh(); a case where a resumed acquire then release leaves no lock.

findings.issue: refresh re-records a lock whose recorded pid is still alive whenever it differs from the asking process, so a live run's release is refused as taken over and the lock can read dead while that run still works the phase.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.10-b6f (a87c0cf0): Re-record only when the recorded holder is gone or no pid is recorded; a live recorded pid stays and is reported; an allow/deny pair.

findings.issue: The line says resume's acquire meets the dead holder as exit 4 and a human-confirmed takeover, which holds only for a different session id; the same session resumed under a new process has its lock re-recorded by acquire with no exit 4.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.10-b6f (a87c0cf0): Name both cases, worded to match the settled acquire behaviour.

findings.issue: The outer handler that gives the lock back also wraps the branch cut after the validated write, so an unexpected raise there releases the lock while the written claim stays.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.10-b6f (a87c0cf0): End the guarded span at the validated write, or restore the snapshot in the handler once the write has landed so claim and lock are undone together.

findings.issue: A new comment says the test module holds that no module reaches a private _locks helper, but the scan covers only scripts/ and hooks/ and test modules still reach private names; the line also overruns the block's width.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.10-b6f (a87c0cf0): Say no module under scripts/ or hooks/ reaches one, and rewrap.

findings.issue: The CLAUDE_PID rule answers ours without the other-session check the token rule has, so with yields a caller of another or no session sharing the holder's pid can re-take a yielding start lock.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.10-b6f (a87c0cf0): Add the other-session check to the pid rule, matching the token rule, with a case.

findings.issue: A hand-typed start in a resumed session over this session's orchestrator lock whose pid is gone gets the re-record's 0, reports took and prints that sign-off or a cancel gives the lock back, but sign-off releases only a start-noted lock, so the lock stays naming the live resumed process; a failed start on that path would also release a lock it did not take under its own note.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.11-b6f (f5fe36b4): Count a re-record as took only when the lock carries the start note; otherwise report ours with a line saying it was re-recorded and keeps its own hold's note so the run that took it releases it, and never undo it on a failed start; separate-process case plus its start-note twin asserting the printed line and the lock file agree.

findings.issue: The docs say a resumed session's acquire re-records its lock under the live process, which holds only when CLAUDE_PID is exported; without it the lock reads dead and meets exit 4, and a start's yielding lock is superseded rather than re-recorded.
findings.resolution: fixed in P106.11-b6f (f5fe36b4): Name the CLAUDE_PID condition and the exit-4 path without it.

review.outcome: [findings: 29 - 1 high, 6 med, 22 low; 29 with a recorded fix commit]

summary:
Several rules the orchestrator prose asked the model to follow are now decided by audit-task start, each with tests:
- Start refuses a task that is not ready.
- Start writes the phase claim with the session id and branch.
- The spawn brief resolves the executor's gate rule.
- The phase claim is bound to the phase lock, and _locks owns the lock's liveness: one public predicate decides whether the holder is gone.

The phase lock follows its session through the whole run:
- A resumed session's acquire re-records its own gone-pid lock under the live process and releases it at the end.
- A start honours another run's live lock.
- The lock stays held through the merge.
- A failed start gives back only a lock it took under its own note.
- Every release message says truthfully who holds the lock.

The prose these rules replaced is either deleted or reduced to one pointer. The rule for relaying a refusal is stated once, in manifest-conventions.md. task.md, status.md and orchestrator.md describe the takeover, refusal and resume conditions as the code decides them.

The review ran six rounds, each lock defect reproduced in separate processes, and every finding is fixed. The phase gate is green, with screenshots and the interactive check, and the invariants check found no breach. Whether the bytes an execution command reads went down across the phase was not measured as one figure; individual tasks reported both increases and decreases.

tasks.description: start reports what a task waits on but never refuses ('REPORTED, NEVER REFUSED' in _locked_start), so readiness is a rule the model only follows. Make start refuse a pending task with unmet references, unless --force with --reason, which the task.start row journals. It reads _status_facts.unmet_refs, with no second copy of the rule. Starting a task by hand for the plan gate keeps working through --force. Delete the prose the rule came from: the term list and the 'Satisfied' paragraph under orchestrator.md's '## Readiness rule'. Keep the heading, which _areas.py and _priority.py cite, and keep the priority and parallel-safety paragraphs. Point commands/next.md step 1 at the ready list and the refusal, document the flags in commands/task.md, and move README.md's Readiness row from the 'Followed' table to the enforced one. Record `wc -c` of commands/next.md and the reference files it requires, before and after. This phase waits for P101's pipeline pilot (P101.1), whose findings decide which prose rules move first.

outcome.technical:
audit-task.py start now refuses a task whose own or phase references are unmet, unless the task is already in_progress (a retry). The check goes through _waiting_on, which reads _status_facts.unmet_refs, so the readiness rule exists in one place. The refusal exits 2, writes nothing, adds no journal row, names each unmet reference as /audit:status spells it (e.g. `P2 (phase)`), and points to --force --reason. New --force flag; VERB_FLAGS["start"] = ("force", "reason"); _start_flags_refusal refuses --force without --reason and --reason without --force; --reason - reads stdin. A forced start writes mode: forced, reason and basis ("unmet: ...") on its task.start row (keys already in _journal_io.DETAILS_KEYS); its summary says FORCED past unmet ...; --json gains forced and forcedReason. An ordinary start writes none of these.
Decisions: a blocked task with unmet references is refused too (the rule is about unmet references, not the status label); --force on a task that is already ready is accepted and records nothing extra.
Docs: orchestrator.md's Readiness rule keeps its heading, priority and parallel-safety paragraphs; the term list and 'Satisfied' paragraph are replaced by a pointer to ready_tasks, unmet_refs and the start refusal. next.md step 1 takes the first READY NOW entry. task.md: argument hint, a --force example, the journal bullet, the refusal list, and the readiness paragraph. README: the Readiness row moves from Followed to the enforced table; the /audit:task row names --force. test__refs.py pf2 lists start among verbs whose hint carries flags (scope widened for exactly that).
Bytes (wc -c), this task's share: next.md 2453 -> 2456, orchestrator.md 57593 -> 57353.
Tests: test_audit_task pr10, pr10b, pr10c, pr11, pr11b replace the old report-only pr10/pr11; pr11c is the allow twin (a ready task starts with no mode on its row; a re-start of an in_progress task is not refused). Red-first proved through the helper at HEAD b6d9a4a3: 715/720 with exactly pr10-pr11b failing. Suites: test_audit_task 720/720, test__refs 304/304, test__areas, test__output, test__deps, test__priority green; ruff clean.
outcome.descriptive: audit-task start now refuses a task that is not ready unless it is forced with a recorded reason, so readiness is enforced by the script instead of being a rule the model reads and follows.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: the refusal reads unmet_refs, writes nothing on refusal, a forced start records mode, reason and basis, the readiness term list left orchestrator.md, and red-first was proved with allow twins

tasks.title: the spawn brief resolves executor.runsGate, and the orchestrator no longer reads config for it
tasks.description: execute-task.md step 3 tells the model to read .claude/audit.config.json through hooks/_config.load() and executor_gate_policy(), and to state the reading in the spawn prompt. Instead, audit-lookup.py brief, whose answer is already pasted into that prompt, resolves it and prints the word with its basis. It calls executor_gate_policy loaded through _loader, the way _gate_feed does, because a script may not import hooks/. An unrecognised value is a refusal, not the default. Delete the prose the rule came from: the bullet 'Resolve executor.runsGate the same way — at spawn, by you' in execute-task.md step 3. The brief bullet carries the line instead. Update audit-lookup's PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md section and regenerate the module map. Record the mandatory-read bytes of /audit:next before and after. It waits for P101's pipeline pilot.

tasks.title: a phase claim yields to a new session when its holder is gone, and refuses only a live one
tasks.description: Fixes review findings P106-R1 (high), P106-R3, P106-R4 and P106-R7. A phase claim refuses a start only while its holder may still be live. When the claim's session holds no live run of the phase - asked through the same lock liveness `audit-lock.py status` answers for `phase-<id>` - a start by another session takes the claim over without --force and records it on the task.start row as a takeover, with the liveness basis and the replaced session in its changes rows. A start is refused, with --force --reason as the operator's way past, only when a live holder exists or liveness cannot be asked; the refusal text names that decision as the operator's before it names the flag. The no-session path (no CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID) is decided and tested: a forced start with no session id keeps the held claim and reports it as kept, never as replaced (R3). The claim's sessionId and the holder comparison use _journal_io.env_session_id(), which bounds and sanitises the value that lands in a committed row (R4). Sign-off and cancel also drop a legacy claim on the index stub under the index lock, so a stub claim cannot reappear after sign-off (R7). Cases: a sequential second session starting the next task of a phase whose previous session left no live lock is a recorded takeover; the same with a live phase lock is refused; the no-session force keeps the claim and reports claimReplaced None; an over-long or unsafe session id is written bounded; a stub claim is gone after sign-off.

tasks.title: every phase claim carries readable liveness, so a takeover never overwrites a live session
tasks.description:
Fixes review findings P106-R8 (med) and P106-R9.

Every phase claim carries readable liveness, so that a takeover never overwrites a live session's claim. When start writes a claim and this run holds no phase-<id> lock, it takes one: a hand-off lock recording CLAUDE_PID the way `audit-lock.py acquire` does, through the same _locks writer. A hand-typed start then leaves the same evidence an orchestrated one does. The orchestrator's own lock (held_by_us) is reused, never doubled. Sign-off and cancel release it as they release the phase lock today; say where, in code.

Until a claim carries that evidence, `none` under another session's claim is read as `unaskable` unless this run holds the lock. That covers a claim pulled from another clone and one written before this change.

A holder judged not live only by the age rule is `unaskable`, not `dead`. That covers no pid recorded, another host, and a probe that answered nothing. `dead` stays for a pid gone on this host and for the empty file an interrupted take leaves.

The takeover line and the summary state the basis itself ("no live phase-<id> lock in this clone"). They never conclude that the holder "holds no live run".

Cases:
- A hand start by session A, with a live pid and no prior lock, makes session B's start refuse.
- A then ends (its pid is gone) and B's start takes the claim over.
- Locks with no pid, or from another host, past the age limit both refuse.
- A claim with no lock at all, from another clone, refuses.
- The orchestrator path (its own lock held) still takes over without --force.

It is taken before any manifest write; held and unforced refuses (_lock_refusal) with nothing written; undo_lock() releases it on each rollback path. _phase_holder returns dead only where _holder_gone sees an end (the empty file of an interrupted take, or a pid gone on this host); every other not-live verdict (no pid, another host, an unanswered probe) is unaskable with a basis saying it was judged by age alone. _claim_plan (gaining an optional phase_id) passes the holder through _holder_under_claim: under another session's claim, none becomes unaskable, the claim possibly from another clone or predating the start lock. _takeover_basis words a takeover as 'no live phase-<id> lock in this clone (<judge basis>)' (or the ours basis); the claim.takeover row, the takeover line and the journal summary use it, and 'holds no live run' is gone. _release_start_lock(git_root, phase_id) releases only a lock whose note is the start's, through _locks.release, from _locked_signoff (after the phase.verdict row) and _locked_cancel (phase kind); the orchestrator's phase lock, held through the merge, is left alone. tasks.title: a lock is given back by the run that holds it, and every release message is true of who holds it
tasks.description:
Fixes review findings P106-R21 to P106-R27. A lock is given back by the run that holds it. A release message tells the truth about who holds the lock.

- _release_start_lock decides on _locks.taken_from alone. Without a recorded takeover from this session, it prints the left-in-place sentence, naming the holder and judge's basis, whether judge reads the holder as live, aged or foreign. release_refusal's takeover sentence is kept for a lock that records taking over from this session.
- acquire's refresh branch, when handed off (the CLI and orchestrator path), treats re-recording its own session's gone-pid lock as this call's hold. It returns 0, carries the token, and says the lock was re-recorded from a pid that is gone, so the resumed run's release at the end gives it back. Callers that are not handed off, and refresh(), keep already-yours.
- refresh() re-records only when the recorded holder is gone or no pid is recorded. A live recorded pid is left as it is and reported.
- start's guarded span ends at the validated write. If something raises after the write has landed, the snapshot is restored together with the lock, so a claim never stays without its lock.
- held_by_us's CLAUDE_PID rule also requires that the caller is not another session, matching the token rule.
- status.md's resume line names both cases. A different session meets exit 4 and a human-confirmed takeover. The same session resumed under a new process has its own lock re-recorded by the acquire and released by that run at the end.
- audit-lock.py's comment says that no module under scripts/ or hooks/ reaches a private _locks helper, and is rewrapped to the block's width.

Cases, each with its twin, driven in separate processes:
- a pid-less aged start lock and a foreign-host start lock each get the left-in-place wording;
- a resumed acquire followed by release leaves no lock;
- refresh over a live recorded pid leaves it unchanged;
- a raise after the write restores the claim and the lock together;
- another session sharing the holder's pid is not ours.

outcome.technical: _locks.py: held_by_us's CLAUDE_PID rule now also requires that the caller is not another session. A yielding claim is replaced only by a caller naming the claim's own session. _rerecord takes taken=: a handed-off acquire that re-records its own session's lock from a gone pid returns 0, carries the token, and says the claim was re-recorded from a gone pid and is to be released at the end of the run, while callers that are not handed off and refresh() still get already-yours. refresh() leaves a recorded pid that is not gone in place and reports judge's basis, re-recording only a gone holder or a pid-less claim. audit-task.py: _release_start_lock decides on _locks.taken_from alone and otherwise says the lock was left in place, naming the holder by session, pid or host with judge's basis. start's outer handler restores the snapshot and then gives the lock back for any raise once the snapshot is taken, the branch cut included. audit-lock.py's comment says no module under scripts/ or hooks/ other than _locks.py reaches a private _locks helper, rewrapped. status.md's resume sentence names both cases: a different session meets exit 4 and a human-confirmed takeover, while the same session under a new process has its lock re-recorded by its acquire and releases it at the end. orchestrator.md's Release paragraph says a resumed run's acquire answers acquired, so that run releases the lock too. Every reviewer case reproduced red at HEAD as a separate-process test: lv13 and lv14 (pid-less aged and foreign-host locks), lv16 (resumed run), lv18 (live-pid refresh), lv19 (no-session re-take), plus lv20 (a session sharing the holder's pid through start). Red-first was proved on test__locks (rf2, rf8, rf10) and test_audit_task (lv13, lv14, lv16, lv18-lv21). Over-fire mutations turned lv8, lv15, rf2b, rf4, rf9, rf11, rf5 and lv22 red.
outcome.descriptive: A resumed run now releases the lock it re-took, a live run's lock is never moved to another process, and a release refusal only says the lock was taken over when the lock records that.

tasks.title: start reports a lock as its own take only when it is the start's lock
tasks.description:
Fixes review findings P106-R28 and P106-R29. Start reports a lock as its own take only when it is the start's lock.

In _take_phase_lock, a code-0 re-record counts as 'took' only when the lock carries the start note. Any other lock re-recorded for this session, such as an orchestrator's 'phase run' lock whose pid was gone, is reported as 'ours'. The line says the lock was re-recorded under the live process and keeps its own hold's note, so the run that took it releases it. undo_lock never releases such a lock on a failed start.

status.md and orchestrator.md name the CLAUDE_PID condition: the same session's acquire re-records its lock under the process CLAUDE_PID names. With none exported, the lock reads dead and meets exit 4 like any other dead holder. A start's yielding lock is superseded rather than re-recorded.

Separate-process cases, each with its twin:
- An orchestrator-note lock: its pid is killed, a resumed hand-typed start runs, then sign-off. The printed line and the lock file agree, and the lock is still held by its orchestrator note.
- The same flow over a start-note lock: the lock is released at sign-off.
- A failed start on the orchestrator-note path leaves the lock in place.
